title: First-ever device execution of three authored-but-never-run nav Challenges (C24, C46, C55) surfaced 3 DISTINCT TEST-HARNESS brittleness defects — NONE is a product defect, NONE is LVA-008, NONE is a 1.3.12-1078 regression
class: Sixth-Law / §6.J test-harness-vs-product distinction. All three findings are artifacts of running Compose UI Challenges for the FIRST TIME against a real emulator — cold-boot keyguard, exactly-1 node-matcher brittleness, and a missing API-provider precondition. Each was a latent test-side gap that only a genuine device run could surface; each fix is test-harness-side and does NOT alter any product code path.
discovered_by: First containerized-KVM emulator run on the nezha gate-host of three Challenges previously authored on a macOS host that could not boot the container emulator (§6.AH-debt). Their KDocs explicitly state 'NOT yet EXECUTED against an emulator' / 'device-exec PENDING'. Driver: scripts/autonomous-qa/run-nav-challenges.sh.

exclusion_proof.not_lva008: PROVEN — 0 LVA-008 teardown signatures observed in these runs (no "State must be at least 'CREATED' to be moved to 'DESTROYED'" and no "Unable to destroy activity"). The three defects are pre-instrumentation/in-test-body brittleness, not MainActivity onDestroy NavBackStackEntry teardown.
exclusion_proof.not_1078_regression: PROVEN-by-scope — 1.3.12-1078 changes are confined to archiveorg topic/download plus a NO-OP navigation guard; 1078 does not touch onboarding-back navigation, search-timeout handling, or bottom-nav UI. The three Challenges under test exercise exactly those untouched surfaces, so a 1078 regression is excluded by code scope.
exclusion_proof.not_product_defect: PROVEN — every root cause is in the test harness or the device-run preconditions (keyguard, node matcher, absent API provider, wrong content-desc anchors); no product navigation, search, or scaffold code was changed to make any Challenge pass.

ah_debt_cross_reference.debt: §6.AH-debt — the container/VM emulator path does not boot on the macOS authoring host (containerized.go hard-requires /dev/kvm, absent in the podman applehv VM; no HVF passthrough).
ah_debt_cross_reference.consequence: C24, C46, and C55 were AUTHORED + SOURCE-COMPILED on macOS but their KDocs honestly recorded 'NOT yet EXECUTED against an emulator' / 'device-exec PENDING'. This cycle is their first genuine device execution, on the nezha containerized-KVM gate-host — which is precisely why three first-run brittleness defects surfaced at once. This is the §6.Z / §6.AK lesson in miniature: source-compile is necessary, never sufficient; only a real device run proves a Challenge.

findings.name: Cold-boot keyguard blocks instrumentation attach on the first sub-case
findings.exception: UNCONFIRMED: framework-reported diagnosis (verbatim exception, forensic anchor quote) — java.lang.IllegalStateException: No compose hierarchies found in the app. Possibly an issue with Compose instrumentation.
findings.root_cause: On a freshly cold-booted containerized emulator the lockscreen KEYGUARD was still up when the first C24 sub-case (backFromProviders) attached, so no Activity window / Compose hierarchy was present and Compose instrumentation found no hierarchies. The other two C24 sub-cases passed — they ran after the device had been woken — confirming the failure is a cold-boot keyguard race, not a navigation defect.
findings.fix: Test-harness/runner-side: dismiss the keyguard and issue KEYCODE_WAKEUP before instrumentation in scripts/autonomous-qa/run-nav-challenges.sh (wake + unlock the device prior to launching the instrumented test).
findings.status: RESOLVED — C24 now PASS after the wake-and-dismiss-keyguard preamble was added to run-nav-challenges.sh.

findings.name: Exactly-1 node matcher brittleness — onNodeWithText("Search") matched 2 nodes
findings.exception: androidx.compose.ui.test assertion failure: onNodeWithText("Search").assertExists() expected exactly 1 node but found 2.
findings.root_cause: The bottom-nav 'Search' tab is the start tab, so on launch the Search SCREEN content renders the text 'Search' AND the bottom-nav 'Search' tab label also renders 'Search'. onNodeWithText("Search") therefore matched 2 nodes, and assertExists()'s implicit exactly-1 contract failed. This is matcher brittleness in the test body, not a product defect — both 'Search' strings are correct and expected on screen.
findings.fix: Test-side: assert each tab label is present with count >= 1 via onAllNodesWithText(label)...assertCountEquals/onFirst (presence-not-uniqueness), instead of onNodeWithText(label).assertExists() which demands exactly one match.
findings.status: RESOLVED — C55 now PASS after the matcher was relaxed to a >=1 presence assertion per tab label.

findings.name: Search never reached the MockWebServer because no API-backed provider was configured — legacy single-tracker paging branch returned instantly, so the 25s withTimeout never fired
findings.summary: The test set ApiBaseUrlHolder to a MockWebServer URL but configured NO API-backed provider. With no API provider, the search took the LEGACY single-tracker paging branch, which returned an instant empty result and never issued a request to the MockWebServer — so withTimeout never elapsed and the user-visible 'Search failed' timeout state was never produced.
findings.device_logcat_signature: On the un-fixed run the device logcat showed the search going SubmitClick -> ListBottomReached (the legacy paging path) with no MockWebServer hit and no 25s timeout — i.e. the Challenge's intended timeout path was never exercised.
findings.root_cause: Missing test precondition: an ApiBaseUrlHolder pointing at the MockWebServer is necessary but not sufficient; the search routing also requires an API-backed provider to be present so the request actually flows through the API client to the MockWebServer.
findings.fix: Test-side, honest precondition wiring: seed a dynamic RemoteTrackerDescriptor + ProviderConfig so the search genuinely flows MainActivity -> Nav -> SearchResultViewModel -> withTimeout -> streamMultiSearch -> ApiBackedTrackerClient -> MockWebServer (the path that can actually time out). Plus corrected 2 wrong content-description anchors in the test body: "Navigate up" -> "Back", and the history-dependent "Search history" -> the search action button (the prior anchor depended on prior search history existing, which is non-deterministic on a fresh device).
findings.status: IN PROGRESS — C46 device-validation is running this session; UNCONFIRMED: the post-fix GREEN device run is not yet captured at the time of writing this record. The fix is present in the test source; the device confirmation is pending.

no_guessing: §11.4.6: C24 and C55 statuses are stated as facts (RESOLVED — now PASS) per the device runs that produced the passing results. C46 is explicitly marked IN PROGRESS / UNCONFIRMED for its post-fix GREEN device run because that confirmation has not yet landed this session. The not-LVA-008 / not-1078 / not-product-defect exclusions are stated as PROVEN per the 0-teardown-signature observation and the 1078 code-scope analysis. Nothing is surmised.
lesson: Three Challenges authored on a host that could not boot an emulator (§6.AH-debt) carried 'device-exec PENDING' KDocs in good faith; their first real device execution immediately surfaced 3 distinct test-harness brittleness defects (cold-boot keyguard, exactly-1 matcher, missing API-provider precondition). This is direct evidence for the §6.Z / §6.AK posture: a Challenge that only source-compiled is not a Challenge that ran, and only execution against a real device proves it. All three fixes are test-harness-side; the product navigation/search/scaffold code was not implicated.
